answer: On an attestation graph, trust propagates from trusted seeds through random walks of bounded length, with each edge’s influence capped. A sybil cluster may have many internal attestations yet a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits walk flow across that boundary. Given bounded seed weight and capped edge influence, min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore constrain the cluster’s aggregate voting weight, even if vertices are labeled copper, fable, or knoll.
